Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

## Continual-ARC task family: lattice-cell marker-pair encoding (task-6dfa0abe)
- Confirmed on one demo and an accepted test, zero wrong submissions.
- Input has a regular lattice: full horizontal separator rows and vertical separator columns partition it into rectangular cells. In the demo (17x15), separators r=5,11 and c=3,7,11 create a 3x4 output. In the accepted test (23x14), separators r=5,11,17 and c=4,9 create a 4x3 output. Output dimensions equal the number of non-separator bands in each direction; each output pixel corresponds to one lattice cell.
- Each cell contains a uniform background (demo 6, test 7), separator color (demo 5, test 3), and occasional marker dots (demo color 9, test color 8). Output preserves the cell-background color unless exactly two markers occur inside that cell; then output is color 1. Markers are counted within cell interiors only (exclude separators). Tested output for task input was `[[7,7,7],[7,7,1],[7,7,7],[7,1,7]]`, accepted. Demo output `[[1,6,6,6],[1,6,6,6],[6,6,6,6]]` matches this count-exactly-two rule.
- Practical procedure: locate full separator lines; partition into bands; count marker-color cells in each interior region. Emit background color for counts other than 2, and 1 for exactly 2. Maintain row/column band order. Do not simply mark cells with any dot or use a count threshold other than exactly two; single-dot cells remain the background color.

## Task family: copy the source tile across divider-defined cells
- Evidence: task-6902876b, solved correctly with no wrong submissions.
- Detect full straight divider row(s)/column(s), which partition the grid into equal-sized rectangular cells. Keep divider lines unchanged.
- One cell contains the source pattern on a uniform background; reproduce its non-background marks at the same local coordinates in every other cell (preserve colors), leaving backgrounds as-is.

This output was accepted with zero wrong attempts. Good evidence that even a dense irregular pattern repeats identically across all cells, and cells may use offsets +8 columns and +7 rows here.
